field.description:
The model field the column holds: the attribute for `field`/`reference`, the link attribute field for junction
attribute columns, empty for the system columns

keyPart.description: For a `reference`, `owner` or `target` column: the primary key field of the referenced model it holds

nullable.description:
Whether the model allows the value to be absent. A store may still create the column nullable (see the
multi-version rules of #838: `NOT NULL` is only applied in the contract phase)

role.description:
What a column holds

- `field`: a model field (scalar or JSON)
- `reference`: the key (or one key part) of a linked model (`ModelLink`, `ModelParent`)
- `type`: the `__type` class discriminator
- `extra`: the JSON column keeping the properties the schema does not know
- `owner` / `target`: the keys of a junction row
- `position`: the index of the link in its array
- `key`: the key of the link in its map
- `attributes`: the JSON column holding the link attributes when they have no declared field

type.description: Engine-neutral column type: each store maps it to its own DDL type (`TEXT`, `DataTypes.STRING(n)`, ...)

ForeignKeyPlan.description:
A foreign key constraint

Stores create every table first and the constraints afterwards (deferrable), so self references and cycles work.

onDelete.description: `ON DELETE` behavior of a foreign key

JunctionPlan.description: A junction table: the rows of a `linksSimpleArray`, `linksArray` or `linksMap` relation

ModelPlan.description: What a model reads and writes: its projection of the table

columns.description: Columns the model uses (its fields, references, `__type` and the extra column), in table order

Record<string, Date>.description: Construct a type with a set of properties K of type T

foreignKey.description: Name of the foreign key constraint, undefined when the target is not in this plan or foreign keys are disabled

keySeparator.description: Separator joining the target composite key into the string the model stores

kind.description:
Kind of a relation, from `Metadata.Relations` (the compiler records the aliases as the type they resolve to)

- `parent`: `ModelParent` / `BelongTo`
- `link`: `ModelLink` / `RelateTo` / `ManyToOne` / `OneToOne`
- `linksSimpleArray`: `ModelLinksSimpleArray`
- `linksArray`: `ModelLinksArray` / `ManyToMany` / `Contains`
- `linksMap`: `ModelLinksMap`
- `query`: `ModelRelated` / `OneToMany`, the reverse side of a link: no storage
- `map`: `ModelsMapped`, denormalized copies: no storage

onDelete.description: `ON DELETE` of the constraint, when one is created

target.description: Identifier of the related model, undefined when it cannot be resolved

targetAttribute.description: For a `query`: the attribute of the target model linking back to this model

unique.description: `OneToOne`: one row at most per target

RelationalSchemaPlan.description: The relational schema of the models of a store: a pure function of their metadata

tables.description: Tables in creation order: a referenced table comes before the tables referencing it (cycles excepted)

SchemaLayoutOptions.description: Options of the builder that change the physical layout: two plans built with different options are incompatible

columnNaming.description: `preserve` keeps the field names (quoted camelCase), `snake_case` converts them

extraColumn.description: Name of the JSON column keeping unknown properties, false to have none

foreignKeys.description: Create foreign key constraints between the tables of the plan

numericAsDecimal.description: Map JSON schema `number` to `decimal` instead of `double`

SchemaWarning.description: A warning raised while building, for the store to log

models.description: For a model table: every model stored in it (single-table inheritance)

primaryKeySeparator.description: Separator joining a composite primary key into a string

root.description: For a model table: the model it was declared for, owner of rows without `__type`

Output.description:
A version of the application running against the tables of a relational store

One entry per store, application version and plan hash (`uuid` is `<store>:<appVersion>:<planHash>`), created by
the store at `init()` and refreshed by its heartbeat. Nobody claims the model, so `Store.computeStores()` sends it
to the `Registry` catch-all: the relational store keeps its bookkeeping in a schemaless store, never the other way
around.

Live versions (`status: "LIVE"` with a recent `lastHeartbeat`) are what `schemaSync` protects: the physical schema
stays the union of their plans. `webda <engine> schema retire` sets `status: "RETIRED"`; `schema contract` then
proposes what no live version uses any more.

appVersion.description: Version of the application (`package.json`, or the `appVersion` parameter of the store)

forced.description: The `allowIncompatible` entries that downgraded a `BLOCK` to `WARN` when this version started

lastHeartbeat.description: Last heartbeat of any instance, refreshed with `patch()`

plan.description: The plan of the version: tables, columns and types, keys, relations, indexes

status.description: `LIVE` while instances run it, `RETIRED` once an operator retired it
